title: Fragile X syndrome
summary: Fragile X syndrome is a common inherited cause of learning difficulties. It can also affect behaviour, speech and social skills. It is caused by a section of the FMR1 gene that has grown too long.
inheritance_plain: It is X-linked: the FMR1 gene is on the X chromosome. The changed section can grow longer when a mother passes it on, so the pattern is more complicated than other X-linked conditions. A genetic counsellor talks it through with you.
carrier_meaning: A smaller change, called a premutation, does not cause fragile X syndrome. Many people with a premutation are healthy, though some have health effects of their own later in life. A genetic counsellor explains what a result means.
disease_meaning: Boys are usually more affected than girls. Early support with learning, speech and behaviour makes a real difference, and many people with fragile X live fulfilling lives.
screening: A genetic test can look for a change in the FMR1 gene. A genetic counsellor can explain who in a family might choose to be tested.
suggested_questions: Why is fragile X more common in boys?
My brother has fragile X. What could that mean for me?
What does a test for the FMR1 gene involve?
card_summary: A common inherited cause of learning difficulties. Boys are usually more affected.
carrier_short: A smaller change (premutation). Often healthy. A counsellor explains.
disease_short: Affects learning, speech and behaviour; early support makes a real difference.
care: Child development and learning support services, speech therapy, genetic counselling and family support groups.
